title: Callstack minifier and heuristic runbook player
author: Maya Rivera
release_notes: Adds a compact stack trace normalizer and a rehearsal runner that can validate runbook steps against sampled telemetry snapshots; no behavior change to production alerting. Note: sampled telemetry is scrubbed and access-controlled.
body:
Summary: Adds two complementary utilities to slo-toolkit: (1) callstack-minifier, a deterministic stack-frame compressor that collapses noisy library frames and normalizes addresses to produce stable, short signatures for alerts; and (2) heuristic-runbook-player, a lightweight replay harness that runs runbook steps against a sanitized, sampled telemetry snapshot to validate step applicability, estimate time-to-remediation (TTR), and surface brittle steps before an incident is handed off.
Motivation: On-call handoffs and post-incident reviews are frequently slowed by long, noisy traces and runbooks that assume instrumentation state. Ops teams want compact, stable artifacts to index incidents and a safe way to rehearse runbooks on representative data without exposing PII or high-cardinality secrets.
Design:
- callstack-minifier: walks structured stack traces (symbolized or raw) and applies a rule set: collapse known third-party prefixes, canonicalize inline frames, strip addresses beyond module offset, and emit a short signature string plus an interactive compressed trace for UI expansion. Configurable via TTL-based cache to preserve historical compression mapping for reproducible indexing. Implemented in Rust with a Python/TS thin wrapper for compatibility.
- heuristic-runbook-player: takes a runbook (YAML with sequenced steps expressed as CLI commands or query templates), a sanitized telemetry snapshot tarball, and executes steps in a sandboxed docker-like environment with resource/time caps. Steps run in dry-run mode by default; each step returns: applicability (bool), simulated-output-summary, execution-duration-estimate, and confidence score. The player includes a rules engine to map failed steps to remediation hints.
Privacy & security:
- Snapshot scrubber pipeline included: field allowlist/denylist, k-anonymization for high-cardinality fields, token replacement for secrets.
- All snapshot artifacts are encrypted at rest and ACL-protected.
- The player has a strict permission gate (requires the new slo-toolkit:sandbox-run permission) and runtime network policy to prevent egress.
Implementation notes & changed areas:
- rust/callstack_minifier/src/lib.rs (new): core compression algorithms, known-vendor patterns, and LRU cache hooks.
- bindings/python/slo_minifier.py (new): thin sync wrapper and CLI entrypoint.
- packages/ui/components/CompressedTraceView.tsx (mod): UI fold/unfold integration and copyable signature.
- tools/runbook_player/runner.go (new): orchestrates step execution in sandboxes, telemetry adapters, and the rules mapping table.
- tools/runbook_player/scrubber.py (new): scrubber utilities, default allow/deny lists, and anonymization heuristics.
- docs/runbook-player.md (new): user guide, security model, and runbook DSL reference.
- CI: add integration matrix for snapshot variants and permission gating.
Commits summary:
- 9e3b2f0 feat: initial callstack-minifier rust crate and tests
- a77bcfa feat: python bindings and CLI for minifier
- 5f4d310 feat: runbook-player runner skeleton and sandbox interface
- c231aab feat: snapshot scrubber and example allowlist
- d9a2f7b chore: docs for runbook DSL and security guidance
- e4f1c21 ci: add matrix for snapshot variants and policy gating
Testing & results:
- Unit tests: 94% coverage on minifier core, fuzzing harness for symbol tables.
- Integration tests: replayed 50 archived incidents (sanitized) across three snapshot shapes; the player correctly flagged 88% of steps as applicable and surfaced 12% brittle steps needing instrumentation updates.
- Performance: minifier median latency 1.3ms per trace on CI runner, tail 9ms.
Review conversation (high level):
- Jordan Li (reviewer): "This looks promising. Two asks: (A) Add explicit ACL checks before a player run to prevent accidental use in low-privilege repos; (B) document how compressed signatures map back to original frames for audit."
- Maya Rivera (author): "Added pre-run ACL gate enforced by tools/runbook_player/perm_check.go and documented reverse-mapping mechanism in docs/runbook-player.md section 4. Also added unit tests for mapping validity."
- Elliot Park (reviewer): "Concerned about anonymization edge-cases (IPs in nested fields). Can we assert scrubber test vectors cover major telemetry types?"
- Maya: "Expanded scrubber test matrix with nested-field vectors and added a sanitization log that reports fields redacted (hashed) without exposing values."
- Sanjay Rao (reviewer): "Please add a short rollback/kill-switch for the player in case of misconfiguration."
- Maya: "Added runtime killfile /var/run/slo_player_disable and a feature-flag controlled disable endpoint; CI verifies the kill-switch behaviour."
Approvals & CI:
- After two rounds of fixes the PR received approvals from Jordan and Elliot; Sanjay approved after the kill-switch patch.
- CI matrix: unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), security static analysis (pass), sandbox smoke (pass).
Merge: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-23 by Maya Rivera.
Migration / Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind slo_toolkit.runbook_player opt-in flag; rollout to internal SRE alpha group for 2 weeks.
- Monitor: player run success rate, scrubber redaction counts, and any permission denial spikes.
- Post-rollout: enable on broader org after 2-week review and add per-team ACL templates.
Backwards compatibility & breaking changes:
- No breaking changes to existing APIs.
- New permission required to run player; docs updated.
Follow-ups:
- Add experimental preflight ranking model to prioritize which runbooks to rehearse automatically (ENG-2254).
- Integrate compressed signatures into alert index to improve deduplication (ENG-2210).
Known limitations:
- Player currently supports snapshots up to ~2GB; larger snapshots will be shard-and-stream in follow-up.
- Minifier ruleset will need periodic vendor updates.
Note to reviewers: logs and sanitized example snapshots are attached as artifacts in CI run 2026-02-22-774980 for reproducibility.
Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests with archived incidents
- [x] Security review (static + privacy)
- [x] Docs and migration notes
- [x] Backwards compatibility validated
